task4.title: Task 4: Short Story with 5 Questions
task4.instruction: Read the short story. Then answer 5 questions. You need 80% to pass.

stories.title: The Little Carabao
stories.content: Mang Ben has a little carabao named Bino. Every morning, they walk to the rice field together. Bino pulls the plow while Mang Ben sings a happy song. One day the rain fell hard and the field turned to mud. Bino slipped and fell. Mang Ben ran to help him and pulled him up by the rope. Bino stood up slowly and shook the mud from his back. That afternoon Mang Ben gave Bino a bundle of fresh grass and a clean drink of water. Bino wagged his tail and mooed softly. From that day on, Mang Ben and Bino worked side by side, and the rice field grew tall and green.

questions.q: What is the name of the carabao?
Where do Mang Ben and Bino go every morning?
What happened one day in the field?
How did Mang Ben help Bino?
options: He pulled him up by the rope
He hit him with a stick

questions.q: What did Mang Ben give Bino that afternoon?
How did Bino feel after eating?
options: He mooed softly and wagged his tail
He went to sleep at once

questions.q: What grew tall and green?
Who worked side by side from that day on?

stories.title: Ana's Rainy Day
stories.content: Ana woke up to the sound of rain. She looked out the window and saw the street turning into a small river. "I have no umbrella," she said. Her older brother Ben handed her a yellow raincoat and his old boots. Ana smiled and stepped outside. At the gate she found a little puppy shivering under the fence. She wrapped it in her coat and carried it to the guard house, where Mang Roger promised to keep it warm. Then Ana walked to school. When the bell rang she was dry and happy, and she could still hear the rain tapping on the roof.

questions.q: What sound woke Ana?
What did the street turn into?
Why was Ana worried?
Who gave Ana the raincoat?
Where did Ana find the puppy?
options: Under the fence at the gate

questions.q: Who promised to keep the puppy warm?
How did Ana feel when the bell rang?
What could Ana still hear?
options: The rain tapping on the roof

stories.title: The Lost Kite
stories.content: Joel made a kite from bamboo and old newspaper. He painted a big red star on it. On Saturday he ran to the field to fly it, but the wind was too strong. The string slipped from his hand and the kite sailed over the mango trees. Joel chased it for a long time. He found it caught on the branches of the tallest tree, its tail torn but still whole. He climbed the low branches and pulled it down carefully. That evening he fixed the tail with tape and tied a stronger string. The next day his kite rose higher than ever before.

questions.q: What was Joel's kite made of?
What did Joel paint on the kite?
Why did the string slip from Joel's hand?
Where did the kite land?
options: In the middle of the field

questions.q: What part of the kite was torn?
How did Joel fix the kite?
options: He asked his father to make one
He used tape and a stronger string

questions.q: When did Joel fix the kite?
What happened the next day?
options: The kite rose higher than ever

stories.title: Market Day
stories.content: Lita helped her mother at the market every Saturday. They carried a basket of eggs, a bundle of kangkong, and a bag of ripe tomatoes. The market was noisy: vendors called out their prices and buyers bargained for a better deal. Lita counted the coins carefully and put them in her apron pocket. By noon their tomatoes were gone and only a few eggs were left. Her mother bought a small mango for Lita as a reward. Walking home, Lita carried the basket on one arm and held her mother's hand with the other. She was tired, but she was proud of the coins she had counted.

questions.q: When does Lita help at the market?
What did Lita and her mother bring to the market?
What was the market like?
What did Lita do with the coins?
options: She counted them and put them in her pocket

questions.q: What was nearly gone by noon?
What did her mother buy for Lita?
How did they carry things home?
options: Lita carried the basket and held her mother's hand
They left everything at the market

questions.q: How did Lita feel at the end?

stories.title: The Mango Tree in Our Yard
stories.content: Grandfather planted a mango tree in our yard before I was born. Every year it grew taller and wider. By April its branches were heavy with green mangoes. Grandfather would tie a net to a long bamboo pole and pick the fruit without bruising it. We gathered the mangoes in a basin and my mother sliced them for the table. Some were sour, so she soaked them in salt water. The sweetest ones we ate fresh with rice. When Grandfather could no longer climb the stool, I picked the mangoes for him. He would smile and say, "The tree remembers who cares for it."

questions.q: Who planted the mango tree?
When are the branches heavy with mangoes?
How did Grandfather pick the mangoes?
options: He tied a net to a long bamboo pole

questions.q: What did the mother do with the sour mangoes?
options: She soaked them in salt water
She fed them to the chickens

questions.q: How did they eat the sweetest mangoes?
Why could Grandfather no longer pick mangoes himself?
options: He was too old and weak
He was sick with a cold

questions.q: Who picked the mangoes for Grandfather?
What did Grandfather always say?
options: We should cut the tree down
The tree remembers who cares for it
Next year it will not fruit
